newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK airlines cancel flights after engine faults.
newsitem.headline: HK airlines cancel flights after engine faults.

text.p: Hong Kong's two airlines said they suspended a total of 15 Airbus Industrie A330-300 aircraft on Saturday, leading to the cancellation of 23 flights.
Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd suspended 11 aircraft and Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd (Dragonair) suspended four, both due to concerns about the reliability of their Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engines.

A spokeswoman from Cathay, the territory's flag carrier, said it is cancelling six flights from Hong Kong to destinations including Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei and Jakarta, and expects to cancel another 10 returning to the territory on Saturday. Some other flights were being rescheduled.

A spokeswoman from Dragonair said the carrier had cancelled seven flights and rescheduled eight others on Saturday. Passengers from the cancelled flights were being rebooked onto other airlines, she said.
She gave no further information on the affected flights.
Anthony Philips, another spokesman for Dragonair, told Reuters the suspended aircraft mainly served routes to Beijing, Shanghai, Kaohsiung and Xiamen.
The Dragonair spokeswoman said the suspension also led to the downgrading of seats for some passengers.
Swire Pacific Ltd and Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd together hold about 26 percent of Dragonair, whose major shareholder is China National Aviation Corp.

The two carriers said they took the precaution of suspending A330-300 operations until the engine manufacturer can provide sufficient assurance that the reliability problems of the engine are resolved.
The decision followed the failure of a Trent 700 engine on a Dragonair A330 on Friday.
Flight KA/MH061 from Hong Kong made an emergency landing on one of its two engines at Subic Bay in the Philippines after developing engine trouble en route to Kota Kinabalu in Malaysia.
It was the latest in a series of single-engine landings by Airbus A330-300 planes from the two airlines.
Cathay's engineering director Rowland Fairfield said the aircraft could be grounded for weeks.
"It's difficult to predict precisely, anywhere between a few days and a few weeks," he told local radio.
Problems in the Trent 700 engines have forced a series of unscheduled single-engine landings recently.
The airlines said the problem with an engine part in the Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engine had been "clearly identified and understood" and a long-term design solution had been found.
But the design will have to be endurance tested before it can be released for service, the carriers said.
In contrast to the two carriers' concerns, Indonesia's flag carrier Garuda Indonesia said on Saturday it intends to continue flying its six A330-300 aircraft which have the same engines.
